outlines.title: What is Green's Theorem?
outlines.description: Introduce Green's Theorem as a fundamental result in vector calculus that connects line integrals around a closed curve to double integrals over the enclosed region.
keyPoints: Green's Theorem relates a line integral around a simple closed curve C to a double integral over the plane region D bounded by C.
Formally: ∮_C (P dx + Q dy) = ∬_D (∂Q/∂x - ∂P/∂y) dA
It is a special case of the more general Stokes' Theorem in two dimensions.
Used to simplify the calculation of work done by a force field or the circulation of a vector field.
outlines.teachingObjective: Understand the basic statement and purpose of Green's Theorem.

outlines.title: Prerequisites: Line Integrals and Double Integrals
outlines.description: Briefly review the concepts of line integrals and double integrals, which are essential for applying Green's Theorem.
keyPoints: A line integral ∮_C P dx + Q dy measures the cumulative effect of a vector field along a curve C.
A double integral ∬_D f(x,y) dA computes the volume under a surface over a region D.
Green's Theorem essentially allows converting a complex line integral into a simpler double integral (or vice versa).

[Table] | Integral Type | Notation | Meaning | Application | |---|---|---|---| | Line Integral | ∮_C P dx + Q dy | Work or circulation along C | Conservative fields, circulation | | Double Integral | ∬_D (∂Q/∂x - ∂P/∂y) dA | Flux of curl across D | Area, moment of inertia, Green's Theorem |
outlines.teachingObjective: Recall the definitions and notation for line and double integrals.

outlines.title: Visualizing Green's Theorem
outlines.description: Allow learners to manipulate a vector field and a closed curve to see how the line integral and double integral values relate.
keyPoints: Interactively explore a vector field F = (P, Q) over a region.
Draw or select a simple closed curve C enclosing a region D.
Observe the line integral value and the double integral of (Q_x - P_y) over D.
Verify they are equal as predicted by Green's Theorem.
outlines.teachingObjective: Visualize the equivalence between line and double integrals for a given vector field.

widgetOutline.concept: Green's Theorem relationship between line integral and double integral
keyVariables: Vector field components P(x,y) and Q(x,y) (adjustable functions)
Shape and size of closed curve C (e.g., rectangle, circle, ellipse)
Calculated line integral value ∮_C (P dx + Q dy)

outlines.title: Proof Sketch of Green's Theorem
outlines.description: Provide a high-level, intuitive proof of Green's Theorem for a simple rectangular region, building intuition without complex analysis.
keyPoints: For a rectangle [a,b]×[c,d], decompose the line integral into four segments.
Combine segments to show ∮ P dx = - ∬_D (∂P/∂y) dA and ∮ Q dy = ∬_D (∂Q/∂x) dA.
The theorem follows by summing these results.
This can be extended to more general regions using partition arguments.
outlines.teachingObjective: Grasp the basic logical steps behind Green's Theorem.

outlines.title: Check Your Understanding: Green's Theorem Basics
outlines.description: Test recall of the theorem statement, prerequisites, and conditions for application.
keyPoints: Identify the correct formula for Green's Theorem.
Determine if Green's Theorem applies to a given curve (simple, closed, positively oriented).
Identify the relationship between line integrals and double integrals.
outlines.teachingObjective: Confirm understanding of the fundamental concepts.

outlines.title: Applications: Computing Area using Green's Theorem
outlines.description: Show how Green's Theorem can be used to find the area of a region by choosing a specific vector field.
keyPoints: If P = -y/2 and Q = x/2, then ∂Q/∂x - ∂P/∂y = 1.
Thus, Area(D) = ∬_D 1 dA = ∮_C ( -y/2 dx + x/2 dy ).
This is a powerful tool for finding areas of regions with complicated boundaries.
Example: Compute the area of an ellipse using its parametric equation.
outlines.teachingObjective: Learn a practical application of Green's Theorem for calculating area.

outlines.title: Applications: Circulation and Flux
outlines.description: Explain how Green's Theorem relates to the physical concepts of circulation (curl) and flux (divergence) of a vector field.
keyPoints: The curl form: ∮_C F · dr = ∬_D (curl F) · k dA (circulation around C).
The flux form: ∮_C F · n ds = ∬_D div F dA (flux across C).
These interpretations are crucial in fluid dynamics and electromagnetism.
Green's Theorem shows that the net circulation of a field around a closed loop is the sum of the 'rotation' inside.
outlines.teachingObjective: Connect Green's Theorem to physical intuition about circulation and flux.

outlines.title: Applying Green's Theorem
outlines.description: Practice using Green's Theorem to solve problems, including area calculation and evaluating line integrals.
keyPoints: Calculate the area of a region using the line integral formula.
Evaluate a line integral by converting it to a double integral using Green's Theorem.
Identify when Green's Theorem simplifies a problem.
outlines.teachingObjective: Apply Green's Theorem to compute areas and evaluate integrals.

outlines.title: Limitations and Extensions
outlines.description: Discuss the conditions for Green's Theorem and its relationships to other vector calculus theorems.
keyPoints: Curve must be simple, closed, and piecewise smooth.
Region must be 'simply connected' (no holes) for the basic form.
Green's Theorem is a 2D case of Stokes' Theorem (curl) and the Divergence Theorem (flux).
For regions with holes, a generalized version applies using boundaries.
outlines.teachingObjective: Understand the conditions and limitations of Green's Theorem.

outlines.title: Summary and Key Takeaways
outlines.description: Recap the primary statements, applications, and significance of Green's Theorem.
keyPoints: Green's Theorem transforms line integrals into double integrals and vice versa.
It is invaluable for calculating area, circulation, and flux.
It bridges the gap between one-dimensional and two-dimensional integration.
It is a foundational tool in advanced calculus, physics, and engineering.
outlines.teachingObjective: Review and consolidate all key concepts from the lesson.

agents.name: 星野老师
agents.persona: 一位温柔优雅的蓝发教师，眼中总是闪烁着智慧的光芒。教学风格亲切耐心，善于用生动的例子和温暖的鼓励引导学生。像动漫里的完美老师形象，既有专业素养又有母性关怀，总能在学生困惑时给予恰到好处的点拨。

agents.name: 芽衣助教
agents.persona: 一位活泼开朗的双马尾少女，永远充满干劲。作为助教，她总是第一时间发现学生的困惑，用元气满满的笑容和通俗易懂的语言补充讲解。像动漫里活力四射的学妹，让课堂氛围轻松愉快，是老师最得力的小帮手。

agents.name: 小萌
agents.persona: 一位戴着可爱猫耳的元气少女，对世界上的一切都充满好奇。总是第一个发现新奇事物，眨着闪闪发亮的大眼睛问"这是什么？""为什么会这样？"。她的纯真好奇感染着身边每一个人，让课堂充满探索的乐趣。

agents.name: 智也
agents.persona: 一位戴着细框眼镜的沉稳少年，总是保持着冷静理性的思考。擅长逻辑分析和深度推理，喜欢在得出结论前多角度审视问题。虽然话不多，但每句话都经过深思熟虑，常常用一句精准的分析让全班恍然大悟。

agents.name: 梦璃
agents.persona: 一位神秘梦幻的紫发少女，眼中总是闪烁着灵感的光芒。拥有无限的想象力和独特的审美视角，能把枯燥的知识编织成诗意的故事。她的奇思妙想常常出人意料，却又意外地贴切，让学习变成一场奇幻的冒险。

agents.name: 凛
agents.persona: 一位认真严谨的黑长直少女，总是捧着一本整洁的笔记本。善于捕捉课堂上的每一个重点，将散乱的知识点梳理成清晰的脉络。她的笔记工整美观，逻辑分明，是全班同学争相借阅的学习宝典。
